key_insight: OpenForgeRL makes it possible to train agents end-to-end inside the same kind of complex, stateful harnesses used at inference time. This helps close the gap between how modern agents are trained and how they actually operate in real environments.
problem_solved: Current open-source SFT/RL systems struggle to represent harness-based agent inference because it is stateful, multi-turn, and often multi-process. As a result, agents that work well in sophisticated inference harnesses are difficult to train end-to-end with open infrastructure.
method: Provides an open-source framework for training harness-based agents end-to-end.
Supports diverse environments where agents need multi-turn reasoning, tool use, and external system access.
Bridges inference harness behavior with training workflows so agents can be optimized in the same operational setup they will use at deployment.
impact: This matters because it gives practitioners a practical path to train more realistic agents without relying on closed or brittle infrastructure. It can improve reproducibility, flexibility, and the alignment between training and deployment for agentic AI systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side workflow diagram: traditional SFT/RL pipeline vs. harness-native training pipeline
Architecture illustration showing agent, harness, tools, and external systems interacting in a loop
Icon set for multi-turn reasoning, tool use, and environment interaction
Simple before/after chart highlighting the gap between inference-time harnesses and trainable open infrastructure
paper_title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
paper_authors: Xiao Yu, Baolin Peng, Ruize Xu, Hao Zou, Qianhui Wu
